neighbours.label: Explanatory discussion of climate drivers, carbon and environmental temperature change
fire: The planet average temperature depends on incoming sunlight and atmospheric carbon dioxide.
Ice core measurements provide evidence of global warming over many decades.
Forests store carbon and influence the climate through exchanges with the atmosphere.
Melting permafrost releases methane that can increase planetary heating.
Changing cloud cover alters the amount of solar energy retained by Earth.
The climate policy aims to reduce emissions from fossil fuel combustion.
Long term temperature variation reflects interactions between oceans and greenhouse gases.
Removing trees changes evaporation and can affect regional rainfall patterns.
quiet: The room average temperature depends on the radiator setting and an open window.
Thermometer measurements provide evidence of local warmth over several afternoons.
Warehouses store timber and influence deliveries through exchanges with nearby suppliers.
Melting snow releases water that can increase flooding in the parking lot.
Changing curtain coverage alters the amount of sunlight entering the office.
The transport policy aims to reduce delays from fuel delivery scheduling.
Short term temperature variation reflects interactions between fans and heating elements.
Removing roof tiles changes drainage and can affect nearby rainwater collection.
